src: Eastmoney: CSI 300 index (000300), China 10Y government bond yield (CN10Y), Shanghai + Shenzhen margin financing balance (融资余额), 30Y CGB ETF 511090 and CSI 300 ETF 510300 weekly turnover. Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: Bond ETF turnover share: 4-week avg minus 26-week avg

notes.headline: Stocks bounce but leverage keeps leaving: margin RMB608bn off peak, 10Y 1.640%; signal +0.87 "bond rally", 9th week
notes.now: Equities bounced today, but leveraged money is still heading out. The CSI 300 rose 0.8% to 4,084 (still 17% below its 52-week high) as small caps and tech led a broad rebound on turnover of about RMB1.64tn, up RMB170bn on Tuesday. Margin financing fell for a 13th straight session on Tuesday, down RMB16bn to RMB2.381tn; it is down RMB22bn since last Friday, RMB160bn (6.3%) over four weeks and RMB608bn (20%) below the June 26 peak. State-linked buyers keep absorbing the selling through broad ETFs (Goldman puts October national-team buying at about RMB170bn), which puts a floor under the index but has not brought leverage back. Bonds gave back a little as stocks rose: the 10Y edged up 0.5bp to 1.640%, still its lowest weekly close in a year (52-week range 1.640–1.892%), and the 30Y CGB ETF 511090 held at 121.46, its highest weekly close since August 2025. The Bond Rotation Signal eased to +0.87 from +0.91 yesterday (+1.17 last Friday, +0.91 four weeks ago) but stays in rally mode for a 9th week since Sep 4, worth 5.2bp so far. Equity momentum (z −1.58) and margin outflow (z −1.33) still drive it, and the 10Y's 4-week fall (−3.6bp, z −0.53) adds a little; bond-ETF turnover share (42%, 4.2pp below its 26-week average, z +0.05) adds nothing. The 26-week stock–bond correlation is near zero (−0.04), so state ETF buying and PBOC liquidity are propping up both sides rather than one feeding the other. Today's drivers were a tech rebound with Asia after the AI sell-off and another RMB1tn of PBOC overnight cash, which pushed short and 5-year yields to new lows, while brokers' warnings about thin duration payoff and regulators' window guidance on bond buying capped the long end. Our read: stay in the bond-rally camp for the next 2–4 weeks, with the 10Y in a 1.59–1.66% range and 1.60% the next target. Rally calls have been right about 80% of the time in the back-test, but this episode has earned only 5.2bp in nine weeks, state ETF buying caps how extreme the equity z-scores can get, and crowding warnings slow the long end, so expect a grind lower in yields, not a gap.
notes.flip: What would flip it: the signal needs to lose about 0.4 z-points to drop below +0.5. The likeliest route is the CSI 300 back above about 4,360 (its level four weeks ago, which turns the 4-week return positive) with the margin balance rising for 2–3 weeks, or the 10Y backing up above 1.675%, which turns its 4-week change positive. Watch the Fifth Plenum communiqué (ends Oct 29), the Oct PMI (Oct 31) and the expected overnight-rate cut (Nov 2); a September-2024-style equity package, or harder regulatory curbs on long-bond buying, would swing the signal toward sell-off within two weeks.
phases: Equities slide, money hides in bonds

The CSI 300 fell 21% to 3,159 (Sep 13, 2024), close to multi-year lows. Margin debt shrank by about RMB160bn, and the 10Y rallied from 2.75% to 2.06%. Turnover in the 30Y CGB ETF rose roughly twentyfold. This is the textbook "asset scarcity" bond bull, and the signal was in rally mode through most of it.
Policy shock: the first big switch to equities

The PBOC's package (rate and RRR cuts plus equity swap and relending facilities) lifted the CSI 300 by 25% in six sessions. Margin debt rose about RMB290bn in five weeks, and the 10Y backed up about 12bp. The signal flipped to sell-off within a week. Because the easing was monetary, the bond sell-off stayed short.
"Moderately loose" pulls money back to bonds

After the Politburo shifted its stance, the 10Y dropped about 42bp in five weeks to 1.62%. Equities and leverage stalled, and the signal posted its best run, an 8-week rally call that was worth about −21bp.

Margin debt climbed RMB630bn (from RMB1.78tn to RMB2.41tn) as the CSI 300 rallied 21%. Funds sold duration: the 10Y rose 25bp to 1.90%, and 511090 fell about 6%. The stock–bond correlation was at its most positive here, so bond prices fell whenever stocks rose. The signal stayed in sell-off mode for 14 weeks and was right.

After margin debt peaked near RMB3.0tn in June, a RMB165bn one-week unwind (Jul 17) began the rotation back out of stocks. Margin debt is now down RMB608bn (20%) and the CSI 300 is 17% off its high as the AI-stock bubble deflates, while the 10Y has fallen to 1.64%, its lowest weekly close in a year. Since late September, heavy national-team buying of CSI 300 and other broad ETFs has slowed the equity slide, and the PBOC's redemption backstop (Oct 26) and RMB1tn daily overnight injections shore up bonds, so the switch is grinding rather than rushing.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows. Margin balance captures leveraged retail and hot-money equity flows. Bond ETF turnover share shows where trading activity is going, not net subscriptions. The back-test covers one rate cycle (Dec 2023 – Oct 2026), mostly a secular bond bull, so the 'rally' side has much more evidence behind it than the 'sell-off' side (44% hit rate, close to a coin flip). Treat a sell-off reading as a cue to cut duration, not to short. Hit rates use overlapping 4-week windows, which flatters them. Not investment advice.
